subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Skull fractures and traumatic CSF leaks: linear to growing fractures, base signs and repair
refs: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 41 (Emergency care of neurologic injuries)

steps.say: A linear skull crack with a normal examination needs watching rather than surgery. A CT scan is ordered to exclude any hidden extradural clot beneath the line. The scan is repeated promptly when consciousness falls because arterial bleeding is expanding fast.
steps.tx: A simple linear **fracture** of the vault with intact neurology needs no surgery, only observation with a CT that excludes an underlying extradural haematoma. The danger is the middle meningeal artery: a fracture line crossing its groove can evolve into a lens-shaped extradural clot over hours. Admit for neuro checks, repeat imaging when consciousness dips, and operate only when a clot appears.

vis.alt: Axial CT showing a biconvex extradural haematoma beside a diagram of a skull fracture tearing the middle meningeal artery with mass effect on the brain.
vis.caption: Skull fracture tearing the middle meningeal artery forms a biconvex extradural clot with mass effect. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A depressed fracture is lifted when the dent exceeds skull thickness or the wound is contaminated. Fragments pressing on eloquent cortex or leaking fluid are also operated. A closed dent with normal neurology and intact skin is left alone.
steps.tx: A depressed **fracture** is elevated when the depression exceeds the thickness of the adjacent skull, when bone is contaminated through a scalp laceration, or when fragments compress eloquent cortex or cause a leak. Surgery cleans the wound, lifts fragments and closes dura to restore contour and protection. A closed dent with intact neurology and unbroken skin can stay untouched.

steps.say: Compound fractures are washed out urgently because infection risk is rising steeply after eight hours. Debridement is combined with tetanus cover and antibiotics spanning skin flora and gram negatives. Closure is delayed when contamination is heavy.
steps.tx: A compound **fracture** needs urgent washout, debridement, tetanus cover and broad antibiotics covering skin flora plus gram negatives, because infection risk rises steeply after 8 hours of exposure. Bone fragments are preserved when clean and viable, while grossly contaminated pieces are discarded. The scalp is closed securely once the wound is clean.

steps.say: A growing fracture is suspected when a childhood skull gap is widening instead of healing. A dural tear has let arachnoid herniate into the line, forming a pulsatile leptomeningeal cyst. Repair of dura with cranioplasty is arranged promptly.
steps.tx: A growing **fracture** strikes children below 3 years when a dural tear lets arachnoid herniate into the fracture line, forming a pulsatile leptomeningeal cyst that widens the gap. The swelling is a trapped cerebrospinal fluid sac, not a simple haematoma. Treatment is dural repair with cranioplasty before the defect grows further.

vis.alt: Neonatal skull showing fontanelles and sutures with scalp-layer diagrams of caput, cephalhaematoma and subgaleal bleeding planes.
vis.caption: Fontanelles, sutures and scalp layers in the young skull where growing fractures occur. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Base fractures declare themselves through bruising around the eyes and behind the ear. Blood or fluid from the nose or ear is examined carefully for a leak. Loss of smell or a facial droop is localising the anterior or temporal fracture line.
steps.tx: A base of skull **fracture** declares itself through periorbital raccoon eyes, postauricular Battle sign, haemotympanum, otorrhoea or rhinorrhoea, while anosmia implicates cranial nerve 1 and facial palsy implicates cranial nerve 7 in localising the anterior or temporal fracture line. These signs are sought in every head injury with a mechanism that reaches the base. Their presence raises the hunt for a cerebrospinal fluid leak.

rows: Blood or leak from ear or nose

steps.say: A suspected leak is tested at the bedside with the halo ring sign on linen. Laboratory proof is beta 2 transferrin, which is specific to cerebrospinal fluid among body fluids. Clear rhinorrhoea after trauma is treated as a leak until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: Post-traumatic CSF **rhinorrhoea** is confirmed at the bedside by the halo sign, a pale ring spreading around blood on linen, and in the laboratory by beta 2 transferrin, which is specific to cerebrospinal fluid, perilymph and vitreous. Glucose testing is unreliable because nasal mucus also contains sugar. Clear watery rhinorrhoea after trauma is managed as a leak until excluded.

left.title: Halo ring sign (bedside)
points: Suggests but never proves a leak

steps.say: Most traumatic leaks are stopping within seven to ten days with head elevation and stool softeners. Acetazolamide is lowering pressure while a lumbar drain is diverting fluid. Repair is indicated when the leak persists beyond fourteen days or meningitis appears.
steps.tx: Most traumatic leaks stop within 7 to 10 days with head elevation, stool softeners, acetazolamide and a lumbar drain, while leaks persisting beyond 14 days or any meningitis episode mandate endoscopic or open **skull base repair**. Antibiotics are reserved for proven infection rather than given as cover. Pneumococcal vaccination is considered once a persistent fistula is proven.

steps.say: Tension pneumocephalus is a neurosurgical emergency that is recognised on CT at once. Trapped air is compressing both frontal lobes apart in the Mount Fuji pattern. A burr hole is releasing the air without delay.
steps.tx: Tension **pneumocephalus** with the Mount Fuji sign of compressed frontal lobes and widened interhemispheric air is a neurosurgical emergency needing burr-hole air release, usually through the same frontal sinus or fracture defect. The trapped air behaves like a mass, raising pressure with deterioration. Relief is dramatic when the air escapes under pressure.

rows: Mount Fuji sign, compressed frontal lobes
